refined_brief: Explain Tag / Recall / optional Find through the belongings scenario and show the small qualitative study observations that motivated the design, keeping the proposed self-efficacy benefit distinct from an evaluated outcome.
source_evidence: Paper pp. 138–140. Qualitative interviews, routine mapping and shadowing involved five adults ages 58–70. Reported experiences: all five misplaced household items at least once a day; three reported medication/frequency confusion; four were apprehensive about tablets or unfamiliar gadgets. Dot counts are participant counts out of five, not population prevalence or an efficacy estimate. Values are in reported-results.csv.
limitations: Existing accepted artwork is reused unchanged, with native text/cues and a new evidence band. The illustration is conceptual, not a participant portrait or original screenshot. Circles/triangles substitute for colour tag cues. No clinical or long-term self-efficacy improvement is claimed.
style: Black linework on white; functional black data marks; no decorative shading
image_generation: No new image generation; existing accepted artwork reused where applicable
